rooms.purpose: Free care and a Park Point beach-cleanup warming stop.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_BEACHSHELTER_F1_HOSTText
lines: You made it down the point! Warm up while I tend your partners.
We leave a kettle on for the beach-cleanup crew, even when the lake is gray.
I came looking for agates. Found three bottle caps and a mitten instead.
The caps go in my litter sack. The mitten gets a place by the kettle. Somebody will be back.

rooms.purpose: A working boat-repair shop; apprentice explains why cedar craft need maintenance.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_BOATBUILDER_F1_HOSTText
lines: I mend cedar boats between freight shifts. Wood swells and shrinks; a good repair has to let it move.
My apprentice is learning to listen for the loose rib before reaching for the hammer.
I named my first canoe OPE. I said it every time I bumped the workbench.
We patched the rib instead of throwing the boat out. It still has a whole lake in it.

rooms.purpose: Optional existing Sulo match and a rowing club with neighborhood stakes.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_BOATCLUB_F1_HOSTText
lines: SULO helps coach the little boats when he is not battling here.
He calls a clean loss good practice. A muddy landing gets a longer lecture.

rooms.purpose: Boat-club winter repair circle; second half of the apprentice story.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_BOATCLUB_F2_HOSTText
lines: This is where we stitch sail covers all winter. Nobody gets charged for the first lesson.
Downstairs, SULO says teamwork wins matches. Upstairs, it keeps your stitches straight.
The boat shop apprentice brought us a crooked canoe cover.
We put it on the smallest boat. Perfect fit! Please tell the apprentice we kept it.

rooms.purpose: Retained native X Defend requisition with a working harbor ledger.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_CARGOOFFICE_F1_HOSTText
lines: The crew needs an X DEFEND for practice. Our requisition desk can exchange one for an HP UP.
The ore ledger upstairs at the warehouse tells you whose work gets these cargoes moving.
Every crate has a weight. Every shift has names.
If the weights make the ledger but the names do not, it is an unfinished ledger. Ask the union hall.

rooms.purpose: Existing food service with a volunteer cook and hotdish conversation.

lines: Our harbor hotdish uses whatever the crew brings. Today it is wild rice and mushrooms.
Someone always asks for the recipe. First instruction: find six neighbors who will argue about it.

rooms.purpose: Existing dock shop with a worker choosing provisions.

lines: I buy supplies before a shift, not after my partners are worn out.
A lake wind does not care that payday is tomorrow. The co-op and I plan ahead.

rooms.purpose: Existing free party care for harbor workers and traveling trainers.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_FIELDCLINIC_F1_HOSTText
lines: Bring your partners in before the next harbor shift. We can rest them here.
Our waiting room is for everyone: deck crews, hill walkers, and the kid on their very first trip.
My MACHOP hauled nets all morning and still tried to carry my lunch.
The nurse told us both to sit down. Apparently I needed the reminder more.

rooms.purpose: A net-mender household remembering the changing seasons on Superior.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_FISHERCOTTAGE_F1_HOSTText
lines: I used to measure a year in net repairs. Now my grandkid measures it in school terms.
We still meet here to mend the spring tears together. A lake can make room for both calendars.
Grandpa says every knot remembers who tied it.
Mine must remember a very confused person. But he keeps asking me back to help.

rooms.purpose: Off-duty foreman sharing credit with the cargo crews.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_FOREMANHOME_F1_HOSTText
lines: At work I count loads. At home my daughter makes me name everyone who moved them.
Try the cargo office, then the warehouse loft, then the union hall. That is the story of a shipment.
Dad brought home a picture of a huge ore boat.
I asked where the cooks were. He went back and got a picture of the cooks. Better picture.

rooms.purpose: Small harbor household with a fog memory.

texts.label: MnDuluthHarborHouse_MN_DULUTH_HARBOR_HOSTText
lines: We could hear the boats before we could see them this morning.
My brother used to answer the foghorn with his trombone. The neighbors still bring it up.

rooms.purpose: Preserved main-story signal receiver with a neighbor maintaining its records.

texts.label: MnDuluthHarborWorkshop_MN_DULUTH_WORKSHOP_KEEPERText
lines: We keep the receiver ready for the harbor signal.
The crews share weather notes, too. The reading hall keeps the older entries where anyone can check them.

rooms.purpose: A hillside seed-saving household with an optional once-only Berry.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_HILLGARDENHOUSE_F1_HOSTText
lines: These seedlings grew in old coffee tins through the last cold snap.
A south window is prime real estate in a DULUTH spring. The cat is filing an appeal.
A BERRY from our windowsill harvest, for the road.
We save seed and share the fruit. Take care of your partners and visit the point garden sometime.
repeat: The next seedlings are not ready yet. Your BERRY was from this year's first harvest. Give our regards to the point gardeners.

rooms.purpose: A compact elder household with local neighborly humor.

texts.label: MnDuluthHillHouse_MN_DULUTH_HILL_HOSTText
lines: The east ramp is easier on my knees. My neighbor shovels it before I wake up.
They insist it was the wind. Most helpful wind I have ever met.

rooms.purpose: A hill trail caretaker remembering an owl call.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_HILLRANGER_F1_HOSTText
lines: I check the stone steps after each thaw. Loose grit makes a fine little sled out of your boots.
The trick is fixing the trail before the first school group gets ambitious.
I heard a HOOTHOOT while we swept the steps. The ranger asked me to draw where it perched.
My owl looks like a potato. My map is excellent.

rooms.purpose: Existing medicine counter and a snow-shoveling customer.

lines: I carry supplies uphill for the older neighbors. They repay me in soup containers.
I own more soup containers than plates. Every lid is from a different decade.

rooms.purpose: Existing party rest and a hostel desk for traveling workers.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_HILLSIDEHOSTEL_F1_HOSTText
lines: Boots by the door, partners by the warm spot. I can help everyone rest.
The early shift sleeps upstairs. We keep the tea quiet and the welcome loud.
A guest from WINONA sent us a bread recipe. The loaf came out shaped like a bluff.
We ate the experiment and kept the letter. That is how a hostel gets its cookbook.

rooms.purpose: Guest stories: one traveler staying to help with the thaw.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_HILLSIDEHOSTEL_F2_HOSTText
lines: I booked one night before the thaw. Then I offered to help clear the neighbor ramps.
It has been four nights. I may live here now.
My postcard says: DULUTH is lovely. Bring another sweater.
I wrote it indoors, wearing two sweaters. Accuracy matters.

rooms.purpose: Taconite interpretation anchored in workers and families.

texts.label: MnDuluthHistoryHouse_MN_DULUTH_HISTORY_HOSTText
lines: This taconite sample came from the Iron Range. Follow it from the mine to rail to ship.
Then ask who cooked the shift meals and repaired the tracks. History needs those names, too.

rooms.purpose: Existing lake equipment shop and a visitor planning a shore walk.

lines: I used to pack for the weather I wanted.
Now I pack for the lake we have. More socks, fewer heroic speeches.

rooms.purpose: A family maintaining a yearly ice-out notebook.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_LAKESIDEHOME_F1_HOSTText
lines: We write the first open-water day in a notebook every year. No contest, just paying attention.
My mother wrote about the birds on the same page. I like her records best.
I drew the gull that stole my sandwich next to this year's ice-out date.
That bird has become an important historical source.

rooms.purpose: Directions to an upstairs weather witness and public reading records.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_LOOKOUTLODGE_F1_HOSTText
lines: Welcome up the ridge. A lookout upstairs has this morning's harbor observation.
Compare it with the old log at the READING HALL, then visit WEATHER STUDY upstairs. They keep the shared record.
I climbed for the view and stayed for the stories.
A sailor downstairs could name every vessel from its silhouette. I could name the snack wrapper in my pocket.

rooms.purpose: First optional harbor-weather witness: a visible fog bank.

lines: I draw the same harbor every week. The roofs stay put; the horizon does not.
Today I used half a page of gray. It still feels like I missed a shade.
From up here I watched fog cover the lower harbor while the ridge stayed clear.
Tell the weather readers: clear on the hill did not mean clear on the lake.
repeat: Still clear on the ridge, fog down below. Take that observation to WEATHER STUDY upstairs when you have checked the reading hall log.

rooms.purpose: Retained native supply service; cooperative ownership explained by a member.

lines: We own a little piece of this co-op together. The boring meeting is part of the bargain.
The useful part is knowing why the prices changed, and getting a say in the answer.

rooms.purpose: Retained second-floor shop and a first-time shopper learning held-item care.

lines: I came for one useful thing for my partner. That was the plan.
The clerk made me read what it does before I spent my allowance. Good clerk. Dangerous to impulse buys.

rooms.purpose: Existing two-battle Metal Coat award and a training-room neighbor.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_MARITIMECOOP_F3_HOSTText
lines: NILS and IVAR run the crew practice here. Their METAL COAT award is still earned in fair matches.
The co-op pays for a place to learn without a badge at stake. Everybody starts somewhere.

rooms.purpose: A retained general store with a shopper buying for more than one household.

lines: My shopping list says POTION, milk, and return Len's casserole dish.
One of those errands has been on the list since February. I am afraid of the conversation.

rooms.purpose: A working freight floor and a link to the upstairs tally keeper.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_OREWAREHOUSE_F1_HOSTText
lines: We tally every outgoing load here. The upstairs clerk keeps the shift notes as well as the weights.
Take the clear aisle. A warehouse is still a workplace, even when the crew welcomes visitors.
I work this loading floor with my MACHOP. We both stop to clear the aisle before the next cart comes.
My partner checks my work. I check the ledger. A good crew catches the little things together.

rooms.purpose: Second labor-history witness: restored names in a shift tally.

lines: The old ledger taught me long division. The people in it taught me to ask better questions.
Numbers are not the whole story. They can help you notice a missing part.
I found a shift listed only as night crew. I asked around until we had every name.
Bring that news to the UNION HALL upstairs. People deserve more than a total at the bottom.
repeat: Every night-shift name is back in the tally. The UNION HALL upstairs recorder will want to hear that.

rooms.purpose: A Park Point gardener sharing cold-frame knowledge and visiting the hill growers.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_POINTGARDENHOME_F1_HOSTText
lines: Sand drains fast. We keep the roots covered and shelter seedlings from the lake wind.
The hill growers save seed in coffee tins. Ask them for a BERRY if you are heading back up.
We planted the same beans in two neighbors' gardens. One plot sprouted a week later.
Our grand experiment concluded that MINNESOTA has a lot of different springs.

rooms.purpose: Existing point shop and a parent preparing for an ordinary long walk.

lines: The beach walk sounded short when my kid described it.
I am buying provisions based on the version with all the detours included.

rooms.purpose: Existing clinic; recovery as a local routine, not just a trainer stop.
A working local pottery household and an apprentice keeping imperfect work.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_POTTERYHOUSE_F1_HOSTText
lines: I make bowls with bands the color of shore stones. No two batches come out quite alike.
My first lopsided bowl holds the shop keys. It has done honest work for twenty years.
I tried to make a mug shaped like a loon. The beak leaks.
My teacher calls it a flower vase. I call it a career change.

rooms.purpose: Existing optional Veska battle and a practiced local explanation.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_QUARRYPRACTICE_F1_HOSTText
lines: VESKA practices here after the quarry shift. Ask for a match when your team is ready.
No badge, no crowd. Just room to try something and learn why it did not work.

rooms.purpose: Public lending room with navigation to the upstairs weather archive.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_READINGHALL_F1_HOSTText
lines: Maps upstairs, stories down here. Library cards are free and wet boots are forgiven.
If you are comparing harbor weather, ask the upstairs reader for the old fog entry.
I borrowed a book about ore boats. My grandma borrowed the same one when she was little.
Her name is still on the old card. I put mine right underneath.

rooms.purpose: Second weather witness: the difference between a forecast and a field observation.

lines: The margin says: Ask the next watch what they actually saw.
That is my favorite sentence in the whole chart collection.
This old harbor log says fog at the mouth, sun on the ridge. A forecast cannot see every shore.
Compare it with the LOOKOUT LODGE upstairs. Then take both observations to WEATHER STUDY upstairs.
repeat: The old log separates the ridge from the harbor. Compare the LOOKOUT LODGE upstairs account, then visit WEATHER STUDY upstairs.

rooms.purpose: Local sailors inviting visitors to the upstairs letter circle.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_SAILORCLUB_F1_HOSTText
lines: The upstairs table is for letters home. We keep extra paper for crews between shifts.
Somebody always tries to fit the whole lake onto one postcard.
First week at the harbor. I can tie the knots, but I cannot remember everyone's names.
The club says that part takes practice, too. They saved me a seat.

rooms.purpose: Letters home and a retired deckhand reconnecting with the next crew.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_SAILORCLUB_F2_HOSTText
lines: I spent years writing home from other harbors. Now I help young deckhands write their first letter.
They keep asking what to say. Start with who made your day easier.
Dear Mom: the lake really is that big. Yes, I have my warm coat.
There. Now she will know which question to ask in the next letter.

rooms.purpose: A Park Point resident keeping storm-washed objects without stripping the dunes.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_SANDHOUSE_F1_HOSTText
lines: The shore rearranged itself again. We move our footpath instead of making the dunes obey.
The little grass roots hold more sand than my shovel ever could.
We keep a box of things that wash up. Fishing floats, old wood, one very clean spoon.
We leave the driftwood homes for the bugs. The spoon has joined the kitchen.

rooms.purpose: A slip-house family with a remembered workboat named after their grandmother.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_SLIPHOUSE_F1_HOSTText
lines: That little workboat is named after my grandmother. Stubborn hull. Excellent name.
She used to bring coffee to the night crew, then stay until everyone had told one good story.
They let me mend nets here out of the wind. I pay rent in stories.
The landlord says the last one was a little short. I have been practicing the ending.

rooms.purpose: A hillside family whose shortcut home becomes a neighbor ritual.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_TERRACEHOME_F1_HOSTText
lines: Going down for supplies is easy. The climb back is how we hear everybody's news.
We stop at three porches, trade two rumors, and usually come home with rhubarb.
I promised to use up the rhubarb. The neighbors heard about it and brought more.
My pie plan has become a neighborhood infrastructure project.

rooms.purpose: Retained tool counter with repair-first advice from a customer.

lines: My shovel only needed a handle. That seemed too small a repair until I priced a new shovel.
The boat builder says the same thing about old boats, with more feeling.

rooms.purpose: Existing optional battle and a crew culture of asking for help.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_TRAININGANNEX_F1_HOSTText
lines: The annex match is a chance to practice, not a test you must pass to belong here.
Good crews ask for help before they get exhausted. Good trainers can learn that habit, too.

rooms.purpose: First labor-history witness: why the hall records names and shares care.

lines: I brought an extra pan of hotdish for the late shift.
Someone labeled it UNION DISH. That makes it sound more organized than my kitchen.
We keep the hall open between shifts. There is coffee, a notice board, and someone who knows your name.
Ask the warehouse loft about its old tally, then visit our upstairs recorder. Numbers should remember people.
repeat: The warehouse loft keeps the shift tally. Bring its story to our upstairs recorder. Everyone deserves a name in the record.

rooms.purpose: A once-only labor-history reward after talking to the hall and warehouse witnesses.

lines: My first shift was recorded in pencil. The clerk still found me in the book.
I thought I had forgotten the crew. Then I read the names and remembered every voice.
The names are back in the record. A little care in the paperwork is care for the people in it.
The crew set aside an ETHER for your travels. You took the time to listen.
repeat: We kept the copy with the names restored. Your ETHER was the crew's thanks for listening.
need: Our hall greeter downstairs and the ORE WAREHOUSE upstairs tally keeper have two parts of a story. Hear both and return. The crew has an ETHER set aside.

rooms.purpose: Public local weather-reading project linking three real interiors.

texts.label: MN_DULUTH_X_WEATHERSTUDY_F1_HOSTText
lines: We compare what people saw, not who guessed the sky best.
Visit the LOOKOUT LODGE upstairs and the READING HALL upstairs. Our upstairs reader will put the two accounts together.
I predicted sun because I wanted a picnic.
Now I write my observations in one column and my wishes in another. The picnic still has its column.

rooms.purpose: A once-only weather study reward for comparing the current lookout and old public log.

lines: Nobody here can promise tomorrow's sky. We can promise to keep our observations where others can check them.
That is why a public reading room belongs in a harbor town.
A clear ridge and a foggy harbor can share one morning. Your two accounts belong together.
Take this MINT BERRY for the road. Keep asking people what they saw before trusting a neat answer.
repeat: Your two accounts are filed together. Keep the MINT BERRY handy for a sleepy partner.
need: Could you compare two accounts for me? Ask the LOOKOUT LODGE upstairs observer and the READING HALL upstairs reader, then return here. A MINT BERRY waits for the completed study.

rooms.purpose: Dorothy welcomes paddlers at the Root Beer Cabin; repeatable free native party care, with no fee or expedition reset.

lines: Well, come on in! I am DOROTHY. Set your pack down. There is always room for another paddler.
Folks call me the ROOT BEER LADY. I keep this cabin as a friendly stop between the portages.
Rest your partners a spell. Then carry your empty bottles out with you, all right?
We paddled in just to say hello. Then the wind picked up, so we stayed to listen.
DOROTHY remembers everybody's canoe. Mine has a patch shaped like MINNESOTA. It is a very memorable patch.

rooms.purpose: Existing optional angler match with a household learning the Mississippi.

texts.label: MN_SPX_ANGLERHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: We practice here so a young trainer can learn without getting stranded on the river. Ask our angler for a friendly match.
My family keeps a fishing notebook. Most entries say what we learned, not what we caught.

rooms.purpose: One of the existing three native archive records, with an archivist who preserves ordinary lives.

texts.label: MN_SPX_ARCHIVEANNEX_HOSTText
lines: Our record here is part of the three-stop archive walk. The CAPITOL ARCHIVE clerk collects the complete set of readings.
I file lunch menus beside survey notes. Future readers should know that people had to eat between great events.

rooms.purpose: A working river-boat cooperative with a member explaining repair before travel.

texts.label: MN_SPX_BOATCOOP_HOSTText
lines: These are our working boats. The river route is for trainers with their own prepared water partners; we do not run a ferry.
We share repair tools here. An hour spent checking a seam beats a long afternoon bailing water.
We used to label tools with our names. Then someone put EVERYBODY on the good screwdriver.
It still comes back to the same hook. That is the best part.

rooms.purpose: Existing three-record Magnet award; archival work made legible to players.

texts.label: MN_SPX_ARCHIVE_HOSTText
lines: Read our rail record here, the civic museum record, and the archive annex record. Then bring your complete reading back to me.
The MAGNET award is for doing the research. Public records stay public even after you collect it.

rooms.purpose: Existing Capitol records office and Union Depot story direction.

texts.label: MN_ST_PAUL_RECORDS_CLERKText
lines: These are public records. You do not need a fancy title to ask a question.
The fair road is north of town. For the missing freight paperwork, try UNION DEPOT. The clerk there has the actual file.

rooms.purpose: A public reading room for prairie, city and river field guides.

texts.label: MN_SPX_CAPITOLLIBRARY_HOSTText
lines: Choose a field guide by where you are going, then read the notes from people who live there.
A prairie, a city garden, and a northern portage each ask different things of a traveler.
I am helping my aunt learn the bird names she hears in English. She is helping me with the names she grew up using.
Our notebook has two columns and a lot of laughing in the margins.

rooms.purpose: Retained three river-measurement Mystic Water award and city flood history.

texts.label: MN_SPX_RIVER_HOSTText
lines: The three river measurement posts tell one story together. Read them all, then come back for our MYSTIC WATER award.
A river is a neighbor with a very long memory. We keep the old flood marks where everyone can read them.

rooms.purpose: A neighborhood meeting room and coat-drive sorting stop.

texts.label: MN_SPX_COMMUNITYHALL_HOSTText
lines: The meeting starts after the coat sorting. Bring a question, or just help us find matching mittens.
Our best motions usually begin with: Who already knows how to fix this?
We put spare mittens in pairs. Nobody has to explain why they need a pair.
One box is all left hands. Somewhere out there is the most optimistic box of right hands.

rooms.purpose: Retained free party care and PC at an east-bank neighborhood clinic.

texts.label: MN_SPX_EAST_AID_NURSEText
lines: Come in and let your partners rest. The care is free, and the PC is here if you need to change your traveling team.
The east-bank neighbors keep this stop ready for people crossing the river.

rooms.purpose: Existing optional workshop battle and a repair-first craft lesson.

texts.label: MN_SPX_EASTWORKSHOP_HOSTText
lines: Our workshop match is optional. The trainer is happy to practice when you are ready.
I fix lantern handles here. Holding onto a useful old thing can be its own kind of skill.

rooms.purpose: A fair crop exhibition staffed by growers comparing soil and water.

texts.label: MN_SPX_FAIRAGRICULTUREHALL_HOSTText
lines: Welcome to the crop tables! Our growers compare what a wet spring did to the low fields and what a dry week did to the ridge.
The best ribbon is the conversation you can take home and use next season.
My beans came from seed my neighbor saved. Their tomatoes came from seed I saved.
Neither of us can decide who owes the other dinner. We keep having dinner about it.

rooms.purpose: Retained Berry snack shop and a family picking provisions.

lines: I am choosing a snack for my partner before the show.
It inspected every BERRY, then looked at me like I should already know its favorite. Fair enough.

rooms.purpose: Existing breeder practice battle; care before competitive display.

texts.label: MN_SPX_FAIRBREEDERBARN_HOSTText
lines: A bright ribbon means less than a partner that trusts you. Brush, rest, and water come first here.
Our breeder offers an optional practice match. Check your team's condition before you ask.

rooms.purpose: A seed-ribbon demonstration with a young maker.

texts.label: MN_SPX_FAIRCRAFTHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: I weave little seed patterns into ribbons. My grandmother taught me to leave enough slack for the cloth to move.
A tight stitch can look neat and still make a poor ribbon. The same is true of a plan.
Mine is supposed to be a sunflower. It looks like a surprised SUNKERN.
The craft teacher says surprised flowers deserve ribbons, too.

rooms.purpose: A public fair exhibition room welcoming first-time entrants.

texts.label: MN_SPX_FAIREXHIBITIONHALL_HOSTText
lines: This hall is for showing what you have learned. Ask questions; nobody expects a first project to look like a tenth one.
An exhibition is better when people explain the mistakes as well as the polished part.
I nearly left my entry at home. Then someone asked how I made it, and I forgot to be nervous.
Next year I want to be the person who asks the new kid first.

rooms.purpose: Retained native mail shop with a fairgoer writing home.

lines: I promised a postcard before buying another snack.
This card now says: Having a lovely time. Please disregard the mustard.

rooms.purpose: Retained food counter with Minnesota fair food debate.

lines: My family divided the fair into snack territories. I was assigned this hall.
I have submitted a request for additional napkins and a smaller committee.

rooms.purpose: Retained garden counter with a cold-frame grower.

lines: I want something for the narrow strip beside our apartment.
The grower asked how much sun it gets before trying to sell me anything. I like this stand.

rooms.purpose: Fair wayfinding that distinguishes the public neighborhood halls from the closed annex.

texts.label: MN_SPX_FAIRINFOHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: The public halls, food counters, and quiz are open. The north annex has its own entry and may still be closed.
If you want to practice, try the breeder barn. For questions, the quiz pavilion will let you try again.
I used to work the information desk. I still give directions when nobody asks.
The clerk made me a visitor badge. It says PLEASE ENJOY THE FAIR. A fair request.

rooms.purpose: Existing three-question SilverPowder prize; corrected host explains the actual quiz.

texts.label: MN_SPX_QUIZ_HOSTText
lines: Ready for three questions about caring for your partners and choosing supplies?
Answer them all correctly for SILVERPOWDER. A wrong answer is a reason to learn and try again, not to stop visiting.

rooms.purpose: Depot freight context without moving the original Team Lode manifest.

texts.label: MN_SPX_FREIGHTOFFICE_HOSTText
lines: The original manifest is inside UNION DEPOT. We keep this desk for questions about ordinary cargo.
Freight is somebody's seed order, medicine, or repair part before it is a line on our schedule.
This parcel is a repaired waffle iron for my sister in WINONA.
The clerk asked if it was urgent. I said that depends on how breakfast is going.

rooms.purpose: Retained cafe service with an artist warming up between studio shifts.

lines: I draw the depot while I wait for my tea to cool.
The trains change. The person reminding me that my tea is cold does not.

rooms.purpose: Retained crafts counter with a maker choosing ordinary useful supplies.

lines: I repair my stage clothes instead of buying a new outfit for every show.
A bright patch can tell a better story than a perfect sleeve.

rooms.purpose: Existing multi-floor market: supplies on 2F and a voluntary trainer on 3F.

texts.label: MN_SPX_EXCHANGE_RECEPTIONText
lines: Welcome to the exchange. The second floor has medicine and BALL counters; the third has a trainer who accepts friendly matches.
Take your time. A useful purchase starts with knowing what your team actually needs.
I walked all three floors before spending anything.
It felt strange. Usually my allowance is gone before I find the stairs.

rooms.purpose: Retained dual native medicine and Ball counters with local shopping context.
Retained optional native battle at the exchange; no gym or badge added.
Retained native general store with local customers.
Retained native free recovery, PC, and four local people with clinic wayfinding.
Retained riverside counter and a canoe-repair volunteer.

lines: I promised the boat co-op I would stop fixing things with borrowed string.
I am buying my own string. We are calling that progress.

rooms.purpose: Retained free native party rest, described as an actual riverside inn.

texts.label: MN_SPX_SOUTHLANDINGINN_HOSTText
lines: Come in from the landing. Let your partners rest while you warm up.
We hear stories from both riverbanks. The best ones get retold over breakfast with permission from the teller.
I was going to rush north this morning. Then the innkeeper asked whether I had seen the river yet.
A journey should have a little room for the place you are in.

rooms.purpose: River survey team explains measurement rather than a truncated exhibition label.

texts.label: MN_SPX_SOUTHLANDINGSURVEY_HOSTText
lines: We compare river measurements from different landings. One reading alone can hide what changed upstream.
The CIVIC MUSEUM has a project using three public posts. Ask there if you want to help with a complete set.
My first notebook had no dates. The supervisor asked when any of it happened.
Now I put the date on the page before I write the clever part.

rooms.purpose: A city garden household sharing space and food between neighbors.

texts.label: MN_SPX_STREETGARDENHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: Our garden fills the sunny gap between two homes. One neighbor grows herbs for pho; another grows peppers for a family recipe.
We spend half the summer carrying little bowls across the fence.
The garden plan said one zucchini plant. It has interpreted that as one zucchini neighborhood.
If you hear a knock, please answer. We are running out of porch space.

rooms.purpose: Existing optional exhibition battle explained as a voluntary neighborhood activity.

texts.label: MN_SPX_SUMMITEXHIBITIONCLUB_HOSTText
lines: The exhibition trainer takes friendly challenges here. You can watch, prepare, or ask for a match.
Our club cheers when somebody tries a new idea, even if that idea immediately needs revision.

rooms.purpose: Existing native Headbutt field note with a reader explaining its purpose.

texts.label: MN_SPX_SUMMITMOVESTUDYHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: Our field note teaches HEADBUTT. Read it with a partner that can learn the move.
Tree study takes patience. First notice the tree, then learn whether it has anyone living in it.

rooms.purpose: A small local press printing neighborhood work and river news.

texts.label: MN_SPX_SUMMITPRESSHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: We print river news, school plays, and the occasional lost-scarf notice.
The most popular issue had the bridge work schedule and a recipe for rhubarb bars on the same sheet.
The printer let me correct a letter I sent in.
It turns out a very strong opinion still needs the street name spelled correctly.

rooms.purpose: An oral-history room linking real native Union Depot service to ordinary railway lives.

texts.label: MN_SPX_TRANSITHERITAGEHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: The public notices in UNION DEPOT explain the train service that is actually running.
Here we collect the stories behind the schedules: porters, cooks, track crews, and the relatives who waited at the platform.
I remember the station by the lunches people carried.
Somebody once crossed the platform with a whole hotdish. We all suddenly remembered a reason to say hello.

rooms.purpose: Existing train service, courier confrontation and manifest; keep every original control program.
Retained bakery counter and a neighborhood regular buying cardamom treats.

lines: My neighbor and I disagree about how much cardamom goes in a bun.
We settle it the MINNESOTA way: bring both batches, cut them smaller, invite everyone.

rooms.purpose: A secondhand field-guide room where annotations connect generations.

texts.label: MN_SPX_WESTSEVENTHBOOKS_HOSTText
lines: These field guides have walked more miles than the shelves suggest.
Check the margins. Someone may have recorded the bird you are looking for on the same trail twenty springs ago.
This guide has a recipe tucked inside the bird chapter.
It is for pancakes. I respect a field researcher who plans the morning properly.

rooms.purpose: Existing optional arena match with a host who explains its voluntary rules.

texts.label: MN_SPX_WESTSIDEARENA_HOSTText
lines: The trainer here offers a voluntary practice match. Rest your partners first, and ask when you feel ready.
A good arena gives you room to learn without making a loss feel like the end of the road.

rooms.purpose: A west-bank neighborhood room with tamale-making and river community life.

texts.label: MN_SPX_WESTSIDECOMMUNITY_HOSTText
lines: We fold tamales here for the neighborhood supper. New hands get a patient teacher and the easy end of the table.
The river divides the streets. Dinner keeps giving us reasons to cross it.
My job is to set out chairs. Every time I finish, another cousin arrives.
We have decided that a successful supper is a chair problem.

rooms.purpose: River angler household: bank access and a family fish journal.

texts.label: MN_MP_ANGLERHOME_HOSTText
lines: My family keeps a fish journal. We write down where we stood and what we noticed, even when we caught nothing.
Cast from a clear bank or a pier. The bridge rails are there to stay on this side of.
I drew a WOOPER in the journal. Dad wrote: caught one excellent drawing.
The WOOPER got away, but the compliment is staying in the book.

rooms.purpose: A staffed information room with correct compact-city clinic directions.

texts.label: MN_MP_ARRIVALINFO_HOSTText
lines: Welcome to MINNEAPOLIS. The clinic is north of the powerhouse GYM in the center.
The department store has five floors. The river library can start you on the mill-plaque walk, if you want a reason to explore.

rooms.purpose: A river painter and a neighbor modeling the local light.

texts.label: MN_MP_ARTSSTUDIO_HOSTText
lines: I paint the same river bend at different hours. The water turns copper at dusk, then the whole picture cools down.
The city is good practice for noticing change without forgetting what stayed.
I agreed to sit for one quick sketch. The painter has spent an hour getting my mitten right.
It is a very good mitten. I may frame just that part.

rooms.purpose: A neighborhood boathouse emphasizing the actual lake piers and river boundary.

texts.label: MN_MP_BOATHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: The lake piers are shared. Our repair table is shared, too, if you put the tools back.
The river rock line marks a closed stretch. A pretty view is not permission to paddle through a barrier.
A school group painted our paddle rack. Every hook is a different color.
Returning equipment has become the one sorting task I look forward to.

rooms.purpose: A binding workshop connected to the existing mill-history plaque activity.

texts.label: MN_MP_BOOKBINDER_HOSTText
lines: I repair the library's field books. Wet covers, loose pages, the occasional very flattened leaf.
Read the three mill plaques along the river, then visit the history hall. A city's story needs all its pages.
I found a note inside a torn guide: Please return this; my sister drew the maps.
The maps were the best part. We repaired it very carefully.

rooms.purpose: A bridge-side home remembering the city through regular crossings.

texts.label: MN_MP_BRIDGEHOME_HOSTText
lines: Three bridges connect our neighborhoods. The middle one meets the powerhouse road.
My morning walk crosses one way for bread and another way for news. I get home with plenty of both.
When the wind comes off the river, everybody suddenly walks with purpose.
In summer we remember how to stop halfway and talk again.

rooms.purpose: A home whose neighborly food exchange points to the real community kitchen.

texts.label: MN_MP_CEDARHOME_HOSTText
lines: Our neighbors cook at the community kitchen. There is warm food and a safe rest for partners.
I sent over one pan years ago. It came back full, and we have been exchanging dinner ever since.
Someone left soup at our door during the cold snap. No name, just a note saying return the bowl whenever.
We returned it with bread. I think we found the right door.

rooms.purpose: Existing native food and party rest with a local communal identity.

texts.label: MN_MP_COMMUNITYKITCHEN_HOSTText
lines: Come in from the river. There is warm food and a place for your partners to rest.
The menu changes with whoever is cooking. The welcome is the part we keep consistent.

rooms.purpose: Existing three-plaque activity directions with a usable public reading room.

texts.label: MN_MP_COMMUNITYLIBRARY_HOSTText
lines: Three mill plaques stand along the river. Read them in any order, then visit the history hall for the complete account.
We lend more than maps here. Ask the quiet reader what they found in a book someone else almost discarded.

rooms.purpose: Existing free rest in an apartment shared by neighboring workers.

texts.label: MN_MP_COOPERATIVEFLAT_HOSTText
lines: We share this room for meetings and a quiet rest for partners. The key rule is to leave it ready for the next person.
Everybody helped choose the furniture. That explains the long meeting and the extremely sturdy table.
I came to one co-op meeting to complain about a draft.
We fixed the window together. Now I am on the window committee, which is apparently just me and a screwdriver.

rooms.purpose: A corner household with real market directions and small-city hospitality.

texts.label: MN_MP_CORNERHOME_HOSTText
lines: The south market sells drinks and BERRIES. The clinic is north of the powerhouse.
We sit by the corner because everyone eventually passes by. Some errands arrive already half discussed.
I am counting how many people say nice weather today.
It is raining. We have reached twelve.

rooms.purpose: Neighborhood courier room preserving the main dispatch story elsewhere.

texts.label: MN_MP_COURIERSDESK_HOSTText
lines: This desk handles everyday deliveries. The print shop is across the river; use the upper bridge when the wind is kind.
A good courier learns which door has a working bell and which neighbor will take a parcel in.
I delivered a letter to the right street and the wrong grandpa.
He knew the other grandpa. We fixed it over cocoa. I am still checking the house number twice now.

rooms.purpose: Retained native department-store floor 1 counter and a shopper making an informed choice.

lines: I start on the first floor and read the signs before shopping.
Five floors is plenty of room to spend money on the wrong problem.

rooms.purpose: Retained native department-store floor 2 counter and a shopper making an informed choice.

lines: The medicine is for a trip with my daughter. She made the packing list.
She put check your partner first above every item. I think she is ready.

rooms.purpose: Retained native department-store floor 3 counter and a shopper making an informed choice.

lines: I compared what our team already knows before buying anything.
Turns out I needed a plan more than another bag full of supplies.

rooms.purpose: Retained native department-store floor 4 counter and a shopper making an informed choice.

lines: My friend and I are making separate wish lists, then explaining each choice.
We have crossed out half the lists. This may be the cheapest afternoon we have spent here.

rooms.purpose: Retained native department-store floor 5 counter and a shopper making an informed choice.

lines: I keep a field notebook beside my shopping list. A machine is useful when the right partner can learn it.
The clerk has the actual stock. I have opinions, which are free and less reliable.

rooms.purpose: Preserved missing-dispatcher story with family members and their native progress conditions.
A lake bird-count room where timing and observation give return visits a purpose.

texts.label: MN_MP_FIELDCLUB_HOSTText
lines: We count birds around the lake. MURKROW visits after sunset, which is why the notebook has a time column.
If two people disagree, we compare where they stood. The lake has more than one good place to look.
I thought I saw the same bird six times. The club asked whether it might have flown around me.
The notebook now says: one very busy bird.

rooms.purpose: A foundry curator connecting the falls to manufacturing and workers.

texts.label: MN_MP_FOUNDRYMUSEUM_HOSTText
lines: The river powered wheels; the foundry made the parts that kept them turning. Neither worked for long without people tending them.
Look at ST ANTHONY FALLS when you leave. The landmark makes more sense when you remember the work around it.

rooms.purpose: Existing Berry gift in a gardener's apartment; no second reward source added.

texts.label: MN_MP_GARDENFLAT_HOSTText
lines: This little garden feeds our partners. The BERRIES I share come from a lot of very patient windowsill work.
A small place can still grow something worth passing along.
I watered the plants while my neighbor was away. They left a list longer than their trip itinerary.
Every pot has a name. I now know them all.

rooms.purpose: Existing native garden counter with a practical pollinator gardener.

lines: I leave a rough corner for bugs beside my tidy flower bed.
My neighbor asked whether I forgot to finish. I told them that was the finished part.

rooms.purpose: A pond-side household growing around an existing shore.

texts.label: MN_MP_GARDENERSHOME_HOSTText
lines: The pond was here before our street. We fitted the garden around the shore instead of trying to straighten it.
The frogs seem pleased. They have not attended the neighborhood meeting to confirm.
We count frog calls from the porch. I made a chart.
My little sister added a column for very loud frogs. It is the most useful column.

rooms.purpose: A grain-records room showing how prairie harvests become river-city work.

texts.label: MN_MP_GRAINEXCHANGE_HOSTText
lines: Each grain receipt started in a field somewhere. Rain, soil, a harvest crew, then railcars and mill doors.
I keep a map beside the figures so a good year never becomes just a large number.
A farmer wrote tell the mill crew thanks on the delivery slip.
We pinned it up where the crew could read it. Best document I filed all week.

rooms.purpose: A city growing room connecting bugs, birds and impatient spring gardeners.

texts.label: MN_MP_GREENHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: We start seedlings before the outdoor beds are ready. A MINNESOTA spring rewards patience, then tests it again.
The flowers outside feed bugs and birds. That is part of the garden's job, too.
I am in charge of turning the pots toward the light.
The seedlings keep leaning back. We are having a very slow disagreement.

rooms.purpose: A neighborhood lake meeting cabin with a child's walking journal.

texts.label: MN_MP_LAKECABIN_HOSTText
lines: The east pier is where our neighbors meet after work. You do not need a grand plan to take a lake walk.
The same loop can feel different when you finally notice what is growing beside it.
We walk the lake every week and name one thing we missed last time.
This week it was how quiet my kid gets when a bird starts singing.

rooms.purpose: Retained native general store and existing local customer.
A mill foreman's home distinguishing family time from the mill office.

texts.label: MN_MP_MILLFOREMANHOME_HOSTText
lines: The office is on the central bank. Here I am off shift, at least until someone asks why the kitchen chair squeaks.
The crew gathers at the community kitchen later. You hear more useful things when nobody is holding a clipboard.
I asked what Dad does at the mill. He gave a long answer.
Mom said: makes sure everyone gets home. That answer made more sense.

rooms.purpose: A mill-worker family whose history stays tied to the river.

texts.label: MN_MP_MILLWORKERSHOUSE_HOSTText
lines: My family worked beside the river for years. The current stayed; the work and the people changed.
The library's plaque walk tells part of it. Our dinner table tells the rest.
Grandma kept her lunch tin from the mill. I carry my art supplies in it now.
She says it is good that it still goes to work.

rooms.purpose: Existing small-stage activity with local rhythm and audience.

texts.label: MN_MP_MUSICROOM_HOSTText
lines: The river keeps its own rhythm. Our little stage borrows the beat and adds whatever the neighborhood brings.
An audience that listens is part of the music. There is room for that kind of practice here, too.

rooms.purpose: A northeast household with real St Cloud directions and generational memory.

texts.label: MN_MP_NORTHEASTHOME_HOSTText
lines: The north gate leads toward ST CLOUD. Our family takes the upper bridge when we head out together.
Someone always remembers a shorter trip from years ago. Someone else always insists we packed better snacks then.
I used to know every shopkeeper on this walk. Now my grandkid introduces me to the new ones.
Knowing a neighborhood is something you keep doing.

rooms.purpose: A local textile studio preserving cultural variety through individual makers.

texts.label: MN_MP_PATTERNSTUDIO_HOSTText
lines: I print patterns one layer at a time. My neighbors bring their own colors and stories to the worktable.
We ask before using another maker's design. Admiration is a good start to a conversation, not permission to skip it.
My aunt taught me a stitch she learned from her aunt. I keep the sample pinned by my machine.
A little square can hold a surprisingly large family.

rooms.purpose: Retained free party recovery, PC and existing clinic visitors.

texts.label: MN_MP_NURSEText
lines: Welcome in from the city. We can rest your partners here.
A busy day of walking counts as a busy day for them, too. Give everyone time to recover.

rooms.purpose: A neighborhood printer connecting useful information to the river city.

texts.label: MN_MP_PRINTSHOP_HOSTText
lines: We print seed-swap notices, show bills, and directions that have to survive a little rain.
The courier desk brings neighborhood news across the bridges. Good printing helps it arrive readable.
My first poster said COMMUINTY SUPPER. Everyone still came.
The next poster had the letters right. The cook said the important part was the supper.

rooms.purpose: Existing held-item gift with a family river-cleanup story.

texts.label: MN_MP_RIVERFAMILYHOME_HOSTText
lines: We found our little gift during a quiet-bank cleanup. A water partner can hold it.
Most of what we carried home was litter. The interesting find was a nice surprise, not why we went.
Our cleanup rule is simple: bring back more wrappers than you took out.
Dad says that makes the snack mathematically responsible.

rooms.purpose: A small river inn remembering mill workers and present-day walkers.

texts.label: MN_MP_RIVERINN_HOSTText
lines: Workers once came for the flour mills. Now guests come for the river walk, and some stay to talk about the mills.
The best inn register has room for where people are going as well as where they came from.
I planned one bridge crossing before breakfast. Three conversations later I had crossed all three.
This city is hard on a strict timetable and good for a walk.

rooms.purpose: A field naturalist explaining actual quiet-bank WOOPER habitat.

texts.label: MN_MP_RIVERNATURALIST_HOSTText
lines: The river joins several habitats. WOOPER favors the quiet banks rather than the loud center of the falls.
Look for the conditions a partner likes, not just the place its name appeared in a notebook.
I drew the whole bank before I drew the WOOPER.
Now I can remember where to look again. My first notebook was just a page of delighted faces.

rooms.purpose: Retained native drinks and Berries counter with a neighborhood picnic shopper.

lines: We are meeting at the lake with whatever everyone can carry.
The list says drinks, BERRIES, and remember the blanket this time. It is an unusually specific list.

rooms.purpose: Retained native co-op counter with a member explaining shared purchasing.

lines: Our co-op buys the useful things together. The meetings are less exciting than the savings.
The one exception was the meeting about whose turn it was to make coffee.

rooms.purpose: Existing Poke Doll advice in a repairer's apartment.

texts.label: MN_MP_TOOLFLAT_HOSTText
lines: A POKE DOLL can help you retreat from a wild encounter. Preparation can be choosing a safe way out.
I repair tools for a living. Knowing when to stop pulling is half the skill.
My partner keeps bringing broken handles here.
The repairer thanks it every time. We may have started a small business without meaning to.

rooms.purpose: A mill-tool repair room explaining water power through hands-on work.

texts.label: MN_MP_TOOLWORKSHOP_HOSTText
lines: The falls turned the wheels; the wheels drove the mill. These tools kept the moving parts working.
An old machine can teach you a lot if you first learn which part is safe to touch.
I asked for the most important tool in the shop. The repairer handed me a pencil.
Measure, draw, then cut. My first good lesson saved a whole board.

rooms.purpose: Heritage room telling Paul Bunyan tall tales while distinguishing camp stories from living histories.

texts.label: MN_BEMIDJI_ARCHIVISTText
lines: Lumber-camp storytellers made PAUL and BABE larger with every retelling. A tall tale is allowed to grow.
We keep those tales beside ordinary camp letters. The letters give the real workers their own voices.

rooms.purpose: Existing native store, clerk and Itasca-trail shopper.

texts.label: MN_BEMIDJI_CUSTOMERText
lines: I am stocking up before the ITASCA trail. Medicine first, then a snack I can eat with cold fingers.
My partner votes for the snack first. We are still negotiating.

rooms.purpose: A border-lakes household treating clean water as a shared responsibility.

texts.label: MN_BEMIDJI_NORTH_RESIDENTText
lines: Our family stories cross borders. So do the birds, the clouds, and most of the water.
We keep a lake notebook because caring about a place should outlast the sign at its edge.
I asked my aunt whose lake this was. She asked who was going to help look after it.
I came back with a litter sack and a better question.

rooms.purpose: Existing free clinic and PC with independent Itasca mark directions.
A shelf-trail neighbor keeps the useful drop and east-climb advice.

texts.label: MN_BEMIDJI_SHELF_RESIDENTText
lines: The shelf trail drops to the road. Use the east climb when you need to get back up.
My neighbor calls that the easy way. I call it the way with time to finish our conversation.
We used to race down the shelf when we were kids.
Now we compete over who can spot the first spring flower on the climb home. I prefer the new rules.

rooms.purpose: Retain the free medic, assistant, native chief battle, receiver gate and survey-restoration story without replacing their programs.
Retained native mart and a visitor choosing encounters versus a quiet road.

texts.label: MN_BRAINERD_MART_CUSTOMERText
lines: REPELs for a quiet road, BALLs for a planned stop at the shore. I pack for the trip I actually want.
Last time I packed for three different trips and could not find my lunch.

rooms.purpose: Outfitter and helper explain lake preparation without implying unearned Surf.

texts.label: MN_BRAINERD_GEAR_KEEPERText
lines: Check the gear before you reach the landing. A loose strap is much easier to fix on this table than in a wet canoe.
Until you can SURF with a prepared partner, the dry roads still make a fine trip.

rooms.purpose: Existing free recovery and witnesses to the falsified lake report.
Preserve the archivist and volunteer evidence about duplicated survey numbers.

texts.label: MN_BRAINERD_VOLUNTEERText
lines: The ranger outside can take your report. Keep your own copy of what you saw, too.
A quiet lake still has things to tell you. Identical numbers on every page do not mean somebody listened.

rooms.purpose: A painter and a visitor interpreting Superior cloud colors.

texts.label: MnGrandMaraisArtistHouseArtistText
lines: The lake changes with every cloud. I paint from the pier at dawn, then come here to see what I missed.
The same shore gives me a new painting every morning. That is a generous neighbor.
I thought I had brought the wrong blue paint.
The artist asked me to wait ten minutes. The lake changed to match it.

rooms.purpose: Retain Dr Tamarack, the original starter/help scene and lighthouse part delivery.
Preserve a firsthand pulse/current witness and add a fisher's family voice.

lines: I mend nets while we compare what the lake did today. A knot gives your hands something to do while your ears work.
Keep the odd observations. They are the ones worth comparing later.

rooms.purpose: Retained native local supply counter and a northern-trail customer.

lines: I buy one extra ANTIDOTE before the long trail. The artist buys one extra blue pencil.
We both call it preparing for the unexpected.

rooms.purpose: Retained nurse care and the existing trail hiker.

texts.label: MnGrandMaraisPokecenterHikerText
lines: Long walks wear out my partners before they wear out my stories about the walk.
NURSE JOY makes us rest. I am working on remembering to do that before she asks.

rooms.purpose: Retained store and a cold-road shopper with useful preparation advice.

texts.label: MN_GR_MART_CUSTOMERText
lines: The road descends, but the cold still finds you. I check my partners before I check my pack.
A good trip leaves enough energy for the walk back.

rooms.purpose: Retained clinic and shift/depot witnesses in the main records story.
Retain the native depot recipient and meter repairer, including original rewards and story gates.
Existing attendant wayfinding and a witness who preserved independent survey copies.
Existing no-forms free care, with a paddler learning to take a break.

lines: I came in ready to explain the whole trip. The nurse said I could sit down first.
Sometimes the best welcome does not start with a question.

rooms.purpose: Keep the diarist's original ICE intimidation evidence and add a family record keeper.

lines: My uncle put dates on every lake note. It seemed fussy until someone tried to tell us what we had seen.
Now I date my drawings, too. Memory deserves a little help.

rooms.purpose: Retained mart and prairie shopper with local supply planning.

texts.label: MN_MK_SHOPPERText
lines: A few POTIONS make a prairie trip easier. I also leave room for the BERRIES a neighbor insists I take.
Planning is useful. Planning for hospitality takes practice.

rooms.purpose: Retained free clinic and a visitor preparing for the terrace climb.

texts.label: MN_MK_PATIENTText
lines: A quick rest makes the next terrace climb easier. My partner likes watching the doors while we wait.
Every time someone comes in, it looks as if the whole town might be a friend.

rooms.purpose: Retain the first-route farmer's ledge/ramp teaching, Berry pickup and Rochester direction; add a farm-family voice.

lines: We watch the bluff shadows move across the garden. My favorite time is when the shade reaches the porch.
That is when the grownups stop weeding and somebody brings out lemonade.

rooms.purpose: Retain the nursery farmer's first-badge acknowledgment, Mankato advice and Berry pickup.

lines: I label the nursery rows before anything comes up. Otherwise we spend spring arguing with the seedlings.
Some wild partners like the tall rows as much as we do. I leave them a little space.

rooms.purpose: Retain the native tool keeper, clear lane, fence-gap return and collectible cache.

texts.label: MN_R02_TOOL_KEEPERText
lines: Tools stay inside so the working lane stays clear. The fence gap leads back to the road.
My rule is to return a tool sharper than you borrowed it. It makes borrowing feel like helping.

rooms.purpose: Retain native full-party free care and the original cabin pickup.

texts.label: MN_R06_CABIN_KEEPERText
lines: Rest here a while. I will tend your whole team; the pine trail can wait.
I keep this cabin open because somebody did the same for me on a much colder walk.
I knit while the travelers warm up. The scarf gets longer every time somebody tells a good story.
At this rate it will reach BRAINERD before I do.

rooms.purpose: Retain June's Lode/canoe sighting and the actual saddle-to-survey-shelter direction.

lines: JUNE asked me to note the wind before the canoe left. I thought it was a tiny detail.
A good ranger keeps tiny details until they fit a bigger picture.

rooms.purpose: Retain Eli, the lake-pier connection and existing road-home cache.

lines: I promised myself a quiet hour at CAMP LAKE.
Then ELI asked how my trip was going. A quiet hour can include one very good conversation.

rooms.purpose: Retain the rest service and Falls circuit check-in, with a trail volunteer.

lines: I help dry the trail maps when people come in from the rain.
A map with soft corners is often one that got somebody home.

rooms.purpose: Retain winter free care and clear distinction from the border report desk.

lines: I mend mittens while the river wind rattles the door.
Nobody needs to tell a heroic story to deserve a warm pair. Coming in was a good decision.

rooms.purpose: Keep the clinic-freight discrepancy witness and add a neighbor who understands practical care.

lines: My sister sorts clinic freight. She knows the difference between a tidy order and the right medicine in the box.
Care starts before a patient walks in the door.

rooms.purpose: Retained mart and a medicine shopper preparing for a prairie walk.

texts.label: MN_RC_SHOPPERText
lines: I keep a few POTIONS for the prairie, then check whether my partners need rest before we leave.
The clerk knows my list by now. I am trying to be as reliable as the clerk.

rooms.purpose: A recovering trainer and a friend preparing calmly for Varel's match.

texts.label: MN_RC_RESTING_TRAINERText
lines: VAREL watches how you use your team. A good plan starts with partners that have had a rest.
The clinic is free. Taking the time to use it is part of looking after each other.
We were going to hurry straight to the GYM. Then my friend asked for a rest.
I am glad they told me. A traveling team should be able to say that.

rooms.purpose: Retain clinic healing, Dr Tamarack's recipient scene and the main freight progression.
Ryan's existing personal Baptism River cabin, with a guest listening to the falls.

lines: RYAN said to listen to the BAPTISM RIVER for a while.
I was going to ask how long. Then I heard the falls and forgot to check.

rooms.purpose: Retained native store, pine-road preparation and original stock.

texts.label: MN_ST_CLOUD_MART_CUSTOMERText
lines: REPELs help when you want a quiet stretch of pine road. I still stop to watch the birds.
Avoiding a battle and paying attention to the forest can be the same kind of walk.

rooms.purpose: Retained free care, PC and granite-path/train visitors.

texts.label: MN_ST_CLOUD_CLINIC_WALKERText
lines: The granite path gives a fine view of the river. My partner keeps choosing the long way back.
We are calling it field research. The nurse calls it another reason to rest.

rooms.purpose: Retain actual Glacier Line dispatch and visited-stop rules; give the waiting passenger a local voice.

texts.label: MN_ST_CLOUD_STATION_PASSENGERText
lines: North toward STAPLES, south toward ST PAUL. The conductor handles the actual route choices.
I bring a book for the wait and never finish it. There is always someone with a better story on the next bench.

rooms.purpose: Retain Dr Tamarack, aide, all three starter balls, original choice and home-town departure progression.
Retain the guardian's original interception, dialogue pages and New Game/home exit story.
The starting bedroom has a cousin visiting before the first adventure, clear of HOME spawn and stairs.

lines: I came over to wish you luck before you head out. I can watch the high score while you are gone.
When you get back, tell me one thing about each town that does not fit on a map. Those are the good stories.

rooms.purpose: Retain the native shop and Driftless Trail Antidote advice.

texts.label: MN_W_CUSTOMERText
lines: An ANTIDOTE helps on Driftless Trail. So does noticing when your partner is tired before you are.
My first trip taught me both lessons. The second one was much nicer.

rooms.purpose: Retain nurse care and the first independent station-readings witness.

texts.label: MN_W_NURSEText
lines: A fresh start is worth a rest. Let us help your partners before the bluff trail.
You do not need to earn a welcome here. Come back whenever your team needs care.

rooms.purpose: Preserve the keeper, delivered-part lighthouse restoration and native signal story.
Preserve all four existing optional native club battles, coach reward and the distinct indoor battle venue.
Preserve the native ICE enforcer battle, captive dispatcher rescue and original records story.
Preserve the native lighthouse keeper, signal prerequisites and North Shore story return.
Preserve Cedar Hollows guide, bluff passage topology, native encounter habitat and existing reward.
Preserve the cave walker, bank passage, native encounters and existing pickup.
Preserve the rock-cut walker, meaningful chamber topology, native encounters and original pickup.
Preserve the mine scout, depot foreman, survey cache and all original main-story conditions.
Preserve the gallery reader, native source cave chambers, encounter habitat and original reward.
Preserve Otta, the native northern passage topology, encounters and original cache.
Preserve Harper, the native shelter chamber, encounters and original Ether.
A dry rock shelter with the original reward and a local lichen observer.

lines: I came to record the lichen at the shelter mouth. Growth that slow makes you careful where you put a boot.
The little chamber above has a supply left for travelers. Take what the trail offers and leave the stone as you found it.

rooms.purpose: A two-mouth northern cleft with its original reward and a passage scout who explains the return.

lines: This cleft has two mouths along the northern trail. I checked both before coming in to mark the dry passage.
The shelf above is a side stop. The low passage connects the two returns. A good shortcut still deserves a look at where you will come out.
